Hi Alice / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a shared record: 

Summary of pain points you described:
- High-traffic support chatbot causing large variance in tail latency during peak hours (~3-4x increase).
- Current infra cost for live inference is a top line concern; need predictable unit economics per 1k queries.
- Compliance requirement to isolate inference for PII-sensitive requests and store audit logs for 13 months.

Goals you outlined:
- 99th percentile latency <= 350ms for single-turn responses at 95% of traffic.
- Sustained throughput of 300 QPS with bursts to 800 QPS for short windows.
- Model must support tool-calling/structured output and be quantization-friendly.

What we discussed we can try: 
- Dedicated pool for the Acme production workload with autoscale policy tuned for peak bursts.
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token compute for repeated context (helpful for support dialogues).
- Model variants: smaller quantized candidate for peeks and a higher-quality variant for critical queries with automatic fallback.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Rishi to share a short technical note with recommended topology, kernel choices, and SLO assumptions (attached).
2) Acme to confirm target P99/P50 & accepted cost envelope so we can size Dedicated commit.
3) Schedule a 90-minute workshop next week for architecture review and canary plan — proposed slot: Tue 23 Jun 10:00-11:30 PT.

Attachments: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (initial sizing + SLO assumptions)

If that looks right, reply with any corrections to the goals or accept the proposed workshop slot and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa — this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our infra/engineering side: 

- Latency SLOs: We currently measure end-to-end response time; for this evaluation please assume model inference-only target P99 <= 350ms and P50 <= 85ms. End-to-end goal (incl. network/edge) is P99 <= 450ms.
- Throughput: 300 sustained QPS is correct; bursts can reach 900 QPS for 2-5 minute windows during promotional events.
- Model requirements: We need function/tool calling, deterministic structured output for top-1 intent, and support for running in 16-bit / 8-bit quantized modes—accuracy degradation under 0.8% relative is acceptable.
- Compliance: Audit logs retention 13 months; we need an option for customer-managed KMS when deployed in Private mode.

We can confirm the workshop slot on Tue 23 Jun 10:00 PT. Also attaching a high-level internal diagram for reference (acme-internal-arch.png).

Subject: Technical deep dive: topology options & SLO assumptions (redwood-slo-proposal.pdf)

Hi Alice / Tom —

Per Marissa's note and Alice's clarifications, attaching a short technical note and a couple of topology options. Key assumptions called out below for quick reference.

Top-level SLO assumptions (inference-only):
- Target P50: 70-90ms (depends on model choice and sequence length)
- Target P95: 180-260ms
- Target P99: <= 350ms for 95% of traffic sample (we treat extreme outliers during promotional bursts with fallback policy)
- Throughput: baseline 300 QPS; burstable to 900 QPS for up to 5 minutes with autoscale/burst pool

Model/quantization guidance:
- Baseline candidate: quantized 8-bit transformer (XXL-lite) with acceptable accuracy delta (~0.6% on intent classification evals)
- Fallback: FP16 variant for high-quality critical queries or when latency headroom exists
- Suggest keeping KV cache warm for sessions to reduce repeated prefix cost (saves ~25-40% CPU/GPU on repetitive dialogs)

Topology options (high level):
1) Dedicated Dedicated-GPU pool (recommended for predictability):
   - Reserved capacity sized for 400 QPS steady with burst pool to 900 QPS.
   - Autoscale policy: add nodes when 85% utilization sustained for 60s; burst nodes provisioned from warm pool (pre-warmed containers) to minimize scale-up latency.
   - Data isolation: network ACL + tenant-level logging to customer KMS.

2) Hybrid Hosted + Private (cost-optimized):
   - Host generic traffic on multi-tenant hosted nodes; route PII-sensitive requests to Private deployment inside your VPC.
   - Request routing at the API layer with policy-based fallback.

Operational mitigations for burst tail latency:
- Canary rollout with 1% traffic to new models, 5% to validate stability for 24 hours.
- Circuit breaker: if P99 exceeds 600ms for >5 minutes, automatically fallback to higher-quality variant in warmed pool.
- Observability: token-level latency traces and per-route dashboards (we'll share sample dashboards in the workshop).

Open questions for workshop:
- Expected average sequence length (tokens) and distribution (median/95th) — this matters for kernel selection and KV sizing.
- Acceptable cold-start window for scaling (30s vs 90s) — affects warm pool size.
- Any regulatory restrictions on shared inference logs or tracing identifiers.

I've attached redwood-slo-proposal.pdf with the sizing table and rough monthly cost estimates under the three topology variants. Happy to walk through these in the workshop — Marissa will send an invite.

Thanks,
Rishi
